summary.text: The candidate with the strongest convergent evidence, CXCR2, is mostly a sign of neutrophil influx. It leads the convergence ranking, with expression, replication, genetics and clinical-stage antagonists all pointing the same way. But almost all of its transcripts in inflamed mucosa come from neutrophils (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), and only a small part of its bulk increase survives composition adjustment (retained fraction [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]). The CXCL8, CXCR1, AQP9, S100A8 and TREM1 increases tell the same story. This neutrophil recruitment axis is druggable but untested in UC, and its genes work best as markers of inflammatory activity.

Behind the influx, some changes belong to the tissue itself. The epithelium loses its metabolic programme: HMGCS2 falls in every cohort (pooled [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.84]) and is also lost as protein ([gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]). At the same time, epithelial SERPINB5 and DUOX2 rise. SERPINB5 keeps most of its increase after composition adjustment ([gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109]). Inflammatory fibroblasts make MMP1, whose increase survives the same adjustment ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.26]), and they are the main source of CHI3L1. These are the candidates that point at a cell type rather than at cell arrival.

Human genetics rarely agrees with the expression leaders. The approved IL12B axis is the positive control: genetically higher IL12B protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), and the result colocalises and replicates in FinnGen. CD274 (PD-L1) rises in the mucosa, yet genetically higher PD-L1 lowers risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]). Blocking it would be the wrong direction; the hypothesis is agonism. CHI3L1, one of the largest and most reproducible increases, has a null MR (q [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=0.577]), so it is better read as a consequence of inflammation than as a cause.

Inflamed mucosa activates TNFa, NFkB, JAK-STAT and TGFb in all eight cohorts. At baseline, higher activity of these pathways is associated with non-response to ustekinumab and infliximab, but it is also associated with non-response in the placebo arm (TNFa placebo padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]). These signals mark disease severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism. Expression of the drug targets themselves (ITGB7 for vedolizumab, IL23A for ustekinumab) does not separate responders from non-responders. The discovery screen proposes stromal first-in-class hypotheses, led by CHRDL2 and CPXM1. Both are made by inflammatory fibroblasts and neither has a drug, but only part of their change survives composition adjustment.

expression.text: The meta-analysis of eight cohorts finds the largest and most reproducible increases among epithelial defence, antimicrobial and neutrophil genes. CHI3L1 rises significantly in every cohort (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.87], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.78e-29]). The DUOX2 maturation factor DUOXA2 ([gene=DUOXA2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.99]), the matrix metalloproteinase MMP3 ([gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.90]) and the calprotectin chain S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77]) rise by similar amounts. These genes report an epithelium under oxidative and microbial stress, matrix remodelling and neutrophil infiltration.

The losses are as consistent as the gains, and they describe colonocytes losing their absorptive and metabolic functions. The water channel AQP8 has the strongest loss ([gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.25]), followed by the tight-junction claudin CLDN8 ([gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.29]). The metabolic enzymes PCK1 ([gene=PCK1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.90]), HMGCS2 ([gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.84]) and UGT2A3 ([gene=UGT2A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.52]) also fall. Losses of this kind are biomarkers of epithelial injury, not drug targets.

Approved and genetically supported targets change only modestly at RNA level: TNF ([gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.92]) and JAK2 ([gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874]). A target's strength cannot be read from its own fold change. OSM rises more ([gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.46]) but with high between-cohort heterogeneity (I2 [gene=OSM; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.965]). The CXCR2 increase holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex ([gene=CXCR2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.552]). Because CXCR2 is an immune-cell receptor, part of that increase may still reflect infiltrating cells (see the cell section).

inflammation.text: Many of the strongest changes appear only where the mucosa is inflamed. In the discovery cohort CXCL8 is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.004], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.986]), yet it rises in inflamed versus non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients ([gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.97]). HMGCS2 behaves the same way in reverse: no change in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.06]) and a paired loss in inflamed mucosa ([gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.95]). Both are markers of local inflammation rather than of the disease state.

A few changes are already present in non-inflamed mucosa and may reflect the disease itself. CHI3L1 is raised in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.84]) and rises further with inflammation ([gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.62]). AQP8 is already slightly lower in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=AQP8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.50]). CD274 shows a small rise there too ([gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.197]).

replication.text: The leading changes from the discovery cohort reproduce in the four microarray and three RNA-seq cohorts. Microarray fold changes are compressed, so the comparison is about direction and significance. The exceptions are informative. REG1A fails in the Leuven infliximab cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]) and in the adult colon RNA-seq cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE165512; layer=rna; cohort=GSE165512; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.259]). AQP8 misses significance in the small Leuven cohort despite a large fold change (padj [gene=AQP8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.169]). In an independent proteomics study, the HMGCS2 loss ([gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]) and the S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749]), DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=1.468]) and MMP3 ([gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]) gains replicate as protein. CHI3L1 moves the same way as protein ([gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]), but the authors did not call it significant. CD274 protein was not quantified.

literature.text: Mechanistic literature on the leading candidates rests mostly on single studies. One study reports that CHI3L1 promotes macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1-mediated NF-kappaB activation, and that inhibiting it was protective. Another reports that IDO1 drives M1 macrophage polarisation through ER stress, and that an IDO1 inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis. AQP9 is reported to act in neutrophils, promoting NET formation and epithelial injury, which agrees with its neutrophil attribution here. SERPINB5 is reported to bind and stabilise MMP9. None of these has been tested in a UC trial.

Biomarker literature is stronger than target literature. Calprotectin transcripts (S100A8) track endoscopic disease activity. HMGCS2 is reported lost in UC with diagnostic value, MMP1 is among the transcripts modified by mirikizumab that correlate with disease activity indices, and CXCL1 and CXCL8 appear in diagnostic signatures. The literature is weakest for the convergence leader. CXCR2 has no verbatim-validated relation in this corpus, and PubTator machine extraction finds only [gene=CXCR2; type=pubtator_relations; source=DATASET:PUBTATOR3_RELATIONS; relations=25] relations in [gene=CXCR2; type=pubtator_relations; source=DATASET:PUBTATOR3_RELATIONS; publications=11] publications, all plain associations, so its literature score comes from Open Targets text mining.

external.text: The approved UC targets act as positive controls. IL12B is the top Open Targets UC target (score [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7424]). It also has the strongest plasma MR result: genetically higher IL12B raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], q [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=1.11e-21]), colocalising with the IBD signal and replicating in FinnGen (OR [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=1.263]). TNF (score [gene=TNF; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6336]), ITGB7 (vedolizumab, etrolizumab) and JAK2 (score [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]) complete the approved set. Genetically higher IL10 lowers risk (OR per SD [gene=IL10; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.071]), and IL10 knockout mice develop spontaneous colitis in MGI. Blood genetics and mouse models therefore agree on IL10 as a protective gene. Among gut eQTL results, higher IRF8 expression in colon raises risk and colocalises (OR per SD [gene=IRF8; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.937]). GSDMA is significant ([gene=GSDMA; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.131]) but does not colocalise.

Expression-led candidates without a UC drug have weaker or contrary genetic support. CXCR2 has Open Targets genetic association ([gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171]) and clinical antagonists in other indications. It has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR could not test it, and that is not evidence against it. It has been perturbed in many mouse colitis papers ([gene=CXCR2; type=mouse_colitis_literature; source=DATASET:EUROPEPMC_MOUSE; mouse_colitis_papers=19]) but has no MGI colitis phenotype. CHI3L1 is null in plasma MR (q [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=0.577]), null in colon eQTL MR (q [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; q=0.275]) and does not replicate in FinnGen. CXCL8 has a weak Open Targets association (score [gene=CXCL8; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1087]). CD274 is the counter-example: genetically higher PD-L1 lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen (OR [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.734]), with instrument heterogeneity (p [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; heterogeneity_p=0.0259]) but a concordant weighted median. Gut eQTL instruments were not available for CD274, so blood and gut cannot be compared. FCGR2A has strong genetic association but a null plasma MR in UK Biobank (q [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=0.916]) and only a marginal combined estimate with FinnGen.

cells.text: Neutrophil genes are the main example of a bulk change that reflects cells arriving rather than the tissue changing. In the single-cell dataset with neutrophils, neutrophils make almost all of CXCR2 ([gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), CXCR1 ([gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]), AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]), S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]), TREM1 ([gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894]) and CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]). After composition adjustment, CXCR2 keeps only a small part of its increase ([gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]), and so does AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.261]). In the neutrophil-free Smillie atlas, CXCR2 is assigned to T/NK cells in one dataset and to myeloid cells in the other, so that attribution does not replicate. Neutrophils also make most CD274 in inflamed mucosa ([gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]). The adjustment can over-correct, because lineage scores also rise when resident cells activate, but these genes are best used as markers of neutrophil influx.

Inflammatory fibroblasts are the second source of leading candidates, and their changes survive the composition adjustment better. CHI3L1 is made mainly by inflammatory fibroblasts (share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652], expressed in [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=80.4%] of them), and the attribution replicates in the second dataset. Neutrophils add a substantial share ([gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466]), and the bulk increase is part tissue change, part influx ([gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.40]). MMP1 is a cleaner fibroblast gene: inflammatory fibroblasts make most of it (share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531]), neutrophils add little ([gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.075]), and a sizeable part of the change remains after adjustment ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.438]). INHBA is assigned to stroma in one dataset and to myeloid cells in the other, so its cell source is uncertain.

The epithelium provides the clearest tissue changes. DUOX2 is epithelial (lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]), and its increase survives adjustment ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.32]). SERPINB5 is classified as intrinsic (retained fraction [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.683]). IDO1 is assigned to myeloid cells in the Smillie atlas, but Xenium inflamed sections place most of it in epithelium ([gene=IDO1; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.inflamed.epithelial=0.371]). It is an interferon-induced gene of both compartments that keeps a significant change after adjustment ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.85]). The HMGCS2 loss shrinks after adjustment ([gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-0.855]). Epithelial lineage scores themselves fall in inflamed mucosa, so this is likely over-correction of a genuine epithelial loss. CDH3 keeps a smaller but significant increase ([gene=CDH3; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.852]). Xenium confirms the neutrophil attribution of CXCR2 ([gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:GSE312420; attribution_by_state.noninflamed.neutrophil=0.818]).

spatial.text: In deconvolved Visium spots, tissue and single cells agree for MMP1 and CXCR2. Inflammatory fibroblasts explain most of MMP1 in situ (contribution [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]), and its high spots are ringed by inflammatory fibroblasts and neutrophils (neutrophil log2 enrichment [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; enriched_neighbors.1.log2_enrichment=1.063]). This places MMP1 at the fibroblast-neutrophil interface of the ulcer bed. Neutrophils explain CXCR2 in situ (contribution [gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.386]), as the single-cell data predict.

For CHI3L1 and IDO1, raw spot deconvolution and single cells disagree, and only the composition-corrected view agrees. Plasma cells explain the largest raw share of CHI3L1 (contribution [gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.258]). The composition-corrected source is inflammatory fibroblasts, which are also enriched around its high spots ([gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; enriched_neighbors.0.log2_enrichment=0.659]), and on CosMx the gene is at background. For IDO1, epithelium explains the largest raw share ([gene=IDO1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.349]), while the corrected source is myeloid. This matches the split between the two single-cell datasets.

pathways.text: Inflamed mucosa activates a broad and highly reproducible set of pathways. TNFa (discovery cohort t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=17.49]), NFkB ([type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=17.48]), JAK-STAT ([type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]) and EGFR ([type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=18.08]) are up in all eight cohorts. So is TGFb, most strongly in UNIFI (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=25.17]). TNFa and JAK-STAT are already targeted by approved drugs. Not every pathway is consistent: p53 is unchanged in the discovery cohort (padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.padj=0.379]), and androgen activity goes in opposite directions across cohorts.

Transcription-factor activity tells a parallel story. The inflammatory regulons STAT3 (discovery cohort t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6]), NFKB1 ([type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=19.75]) and AP1 ([type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=18.4]) are active in all eight cohorts. Meanwhile the intestinal identity factor CDX2 loses activity in all eight, most strongly in the paediatric PROTECT rectum (t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE109142.t=-20.57]), matching the loss of colonocyte genes.

The most specific cell-cell circuits concern neutrophil recruitment, and most are untargeted. These are ligand-receptor co-expression, not proof of signalling. Inflammatory fibroblasts send CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils, a pairing almost absent in uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=3.871]). Neutrophils send CXCL8 to ACKR1 venular endothelium (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=7870.993]). INHBA from inflammatory fibroblasts reaches TGFBR3 on smooth muscle cells only in inflamed mucosa (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=66.463]). The targeted TNF axis links monocyte-derived macrophages to neutrophils through TNFRSF1B (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=80.329]). Macrophage IL1B pairs mostly with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophils (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=4251.623]), a pairing that would buffer the signal. The OSM neutrophil-to-fibroblast pairing through IL6ST is not stronger in inflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]), which does not support OSM signalling as a driver here.

treatment.text: Baseline pathway activity is associated with non-response, but mostly as a marker of severity. Higher TNFa activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=4.84e-05]) and to infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]). The same holds in the UNIFI placebo arm (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]). TGFb follows the same pattern: ustekinumab padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493], UNIFI placebo padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984], and corticosteroid-treated children padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.corticosteroids (PROTECT).padj=0.0018]. JAK-STAT is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not with vedolizumab response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]). None of these is a drug-specific signal.

Gene-level associations show the same pattern. Neutrophil and inflammatory genes are higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders: CXCR2 (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-06]), TREM1 ([gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=4.74e-05]) and CHI3L1 ([gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.00971]). All three also separate UNIFI placebo non-responders (CXCR2 [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126], TREM1 [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234], CHI3L1 [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0203]), so they mark severity. OSM is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=2.64e-05]) but not significantly in placebo (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]). Its drug-by-expression interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]), so a drug-specific effect is not shown. Target expression does not select patients: ITGB7 for vedolizumab (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), IL23A for ustekinumab (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and TNF for infliximab (padj [gene=TNF; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.493]) are all null. In the adalimumab single-cell atlas, treatment lowers IL1B in IL1B-high macrophages (coef [gene=IL1B; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.0.coef=-1.593]) and lowers CXCL8 in cycling mononuclear phagocytes (coef [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.coef=-1.377]). It raises CHI3L1 in fibroblasts (coef [gene=CHI3L1; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.0.coef=2.052]), a hint that the fibroblast programme persists under anti-TNF therapy.

discovery.text: CHRDL2 is the leading first-in-class hypothesis of the discovery screen. It is up in UC (pooled log2FC [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=2.36]), made by inflammatory fibroblasts (share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.39]) with the stromal attribution replicated, antibody-tractable and without a clinical drug. What weakens it: only part of the change survives composition adjustment (retained [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.28]), so stromal expansion explains much of the signal. It also has the highest vital-organ RNA of the shortlist ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6]). Missing: protein data, genetics and any perturbation in colitis models.

CPXM1 is a second stromal hypothesis. It is up in all cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.89]) and keeps the largest share of its change among the stromal candidates after composition adjustment ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.41]). It is expressed in [gene=CPXM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=46.1%] of inflammatory fibroblasts, with the attribution replicated, and has low vital-organ RNA ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=9.1]). Its function in colitis is unknown, and it has no genetic or protein evidence yet.

XKR9 is the only shortlisted candidate whose change is intrinsic to the tissue (retained [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.80], epithelial), which makes it the cleanest epithelial hypothesis. But it is up in only half of the cohorts, so replication is the first thing to establish. The other lymphocyte and stromal hits on the list are largely composition-driven.

integration.text: The streams agree most clearly on three points. First, the approved IL12B axis is supported by genetics, Open Targets and literature, and acts as a positive control (MR OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]). Second, expression, single-cell, spatial and literature data all describe a neutrophil recruitment programme centred on CXCR2 and its ligands, which marks inflammatory activity and severity. Third, MMP1 is consistently placed in inflammatory fibroblasts by single cells, the composition adjustment and deconvolved Visium spots (contribution [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]). The loss of epithelial metabolism, with HMGCS2 lost as both RNA and protein, is the most reproducible biomarker signal.

The streams disagree on several leaders. CHI3L1 has one of the strongest and most reproducible expression changes but a null MR in blood and colon (q [gene=CHI3L1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; q=0.577]) and a modest protein change, so it is a severity biomarker rather than a validated driver. For CD274, expression and genetics point in opposite directions: its rise in inflamed mucosa coexists with protective genetics (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), so the checkpoint blockers in Open Targets are the wrong direction. CXCR2 leads the ranking, but its literature is machine-extracted associations and most of its expression signal is composition. TNF and JAK2 have strong genetic and drug support with small mRNA changes. OSM rises and is associated with ustekinumab non-response, but its fibroblast circuit is not stronger in inflamed mucosa.

targets.rationale: Positive control (ustekinumab target). It is the top Open Targets UC target and has the strongest causal genetic evidence: genetically higher plasma IL12B raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen. It ranks first despite not being an expression leader, because genetics and an approved drug outweigh fold change.

Positive control (approved anti-TNF drugs). It is a top Open Targets UC target, and the TNFa pathway is active in all eight cohorts, although TNF mRNA itself changes only modestly ([gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.92]) and does not separate infliximab responders.

Positive control (vedolizumab, etrolizumab). Its baseline expression does not separate vedolizumab responders (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), a reminder that target mRNA does not select patients.

First in the convergence ranking, with genetic association, clinical antagonists in other indications and replication in every cohort. It sits below the positive controls because neutrophils make almost all of it and little of its change survives composition adjustment (retained [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]), it marks severity in placebo arms, and MR could not test it. It is a druggable neutrophil-recruitment target and a marker of influx.

Made by inflammatory fibroblasts according to single cells, composition adjustment and deconvolved Visium spots (contribution [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]). It has clinical-stage inhibitors from other indications and a composition-resistant increase. It has no genetic support, and broad MMP inhibition carries known tolerability problems.

Ranked above its expression size because genetics gives a direction: genetically higher PD-L1 lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen. The approved checkpoint blockers would be harmful, and agonism is the hypothesis. The gene is not strongly constrained (LOEUF [gene=CD274; type=target_safety; source=DATASET:SAFETY; loeuf=0.476]) and has no curated safety events. Its mucosal rise is partly neutrophil-derived.

One of the largest and most reproducible increases (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.87]), made by inflammatory fibroblasts and already raised in non-inflamed mucosa. It is placed as a biomarker, not a target, because MR in blood and colon is null and it separates placebo non-responders, marking severity. It is antibody and small-molecule tractable if causal evidence emerges.

Positive control for biomarkers: a calprotectin chain, made by neutrophils and confirmed as protein in UC mucosa ([gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749]).

The most reproducible marker of epithelial injury: lost in every cohort and as protein ([gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]), and local to inflamed mucosa.

One of the few leading increases intrinsic to the epithelium (adjusted log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109]), with low vital-organ expression and a reported MMP9-stabilising mechanism. It has no drug and no genetic evidence.

An epithelial oxidase whose increase survives composition adjustment and replicates as protein ([gene=DUOX2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=1.468]). Its biomarker value is clear; as a target it lacks genetics and drugs.

Up in every cohort with a composition-resistant change ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.85]), expressed by epithelium and myeloid cells, and with clinical inhibitors and one mouse study supporting inhibition. It has no genetic support.

Exploratory: the leading first-in-class candidate, a stromal, antibody-tractable gene without a drug (retained after composition [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.28]). It needs protein, genetic and perturbation evidence, and a check of its vital-organ expression.

Exploratory: a stromal first-in-class candidate that keeps more of its change after composition adjustment than the other stromal hits ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.41]) and has low vital-organ RNA. Its function in colitis is untested.

limitations.text: This is the single-agent arm: one orchestrator did the work of the six specialists with the same tools, but with fewer calls per stream, so some candidates have less depth than in the multi-agent run.

The composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated or when the epithelial share falls. Losing significance after adjustment is not proof of pure influx, and the epithelial losses (HMGCS2) are probably under-estimated by it.

Mendelian randomisation could not test several leading candidates (CXCR2, INHBA) for lack of cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instruments. Not tested is not evidence against them. Plasma protein is not mucosal protein, and gut eQTL instruments were missing for CD274 and IL12B.
Treatment associations are baseline associations in modest cohorts, not predictions. Most signals also appear in placebo arms and mark severity, and the adalimumab single-cell cohort is very small.

Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression, not proof of signalling. Most candidates are at background on CosMx, and spot-level Visium co-variation is weaker evidence of the producing cell than single-cell data.
Passing the numeric checks means no failures were detected by the automatic checks; it is not complete scientific validation of the interpretations.
